walkthroughs.body_html:
Changing Cities — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Changing Cities brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Changing Cities.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why is the global energy transition slower than many expect?
options: The transition is slow because people don't want to give up cars.

Existing fossil-fuel infrastructure is sunk cost, low-carbon alternatives need vast capital, intermittency requires storage, and political/economic interests resist change — even as costs of renewables fall.
The energy transition is slow because renewable energy doesn't actually work.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between outsourcing and offshoring?
options: The transition is slow because people don't want to give up cars.
Outsourcing means moving to another country and offshoring means hiring contractors.
Outsourcing and offshoring are the same thing.

Outsourcing means contracting work to another company; offshoring means relocating work to another country. A firm can outsource without offshoring, or offshore without outsourcing (in-house overseas).
